Background High-intensity functional training (HIFT) has become more popular, and the number of practitioners has increased; however, it remains unclear whether perturbations in the immune parameters occur, even after one single bout. Our aim was to examine acute leucocyte, muscle damage, and stress marker responses following a single ‘Cindy’ workout session, and compare the results between novice and experienced participants. Material and methods Twenty-three HIFT practitioners (age 31.0 ± 1.0 years) completed the ‘Cindy’ workout. They were categorized as novice (3–8 months of experience; n = 10) and experienced (≥18 months; n = 13). White blood cell (WBC) count, plasma creatine kinase (CK) activity, blood cortisol level, and lactate concentration were measured. Blood analysis was performed before (pre-ex), immediately after (post-ex), 30 min after (post-30 min), and 24 h after (post-24 h) a single ‘Cindy’ workout session. Results WBC count was higher post-ex (6.8 to 11.8x10 3 /μL) and returned to baseline values within post-30 min (p<0.01). Neutrophil (3.3 to 4.5x10 3 /μL) and lymphocyte levels (2.8 to 5.9x10 3 /μL) were higher post-ex and returned to baseline values after post-24 h, yet lymphocytopoenia (2.2x10 3 /μL) was observed at post-30 min (p<0.01). CK increased post-ex (174.9 to 226.7 U.L -1 ) and remained elevated post-24 h. Cortisol (14.7 to 17.0 μg/dL) and lactate (1.9 to 13.5 mmol.l -1 ) responses increased post-ex, but only the lactate level was reduced at post-30 min (p<0.01). The experienced participants had higher WBC, lymphocyte, and cortisol concentrations post-ex than the novice ones (p<0.01). Conclusions A single HIFT session elicited significant acute perturbations in WBC count, stress markers, and muscle tissue, which is like other similar regimens. Importantly, the experienced participants showed greater lymphocyte and cortisol responses than the novice ones. http://dx.doi.org/10.13039/501100002322 Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior Finance Code 001 https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6524-6691 Gomes João Henrique This study was financed in part by the Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior – Brazil (CAPES – Finance Code 001). extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the acute effects of a single High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) 'Cindy' workout session on immune parameters (leucocyte counts and subsets), muscle damage markers (creatine kinase), and stress markers (cortisol, lactate, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-cortisol ratio). The research compared these physiological responses between novice and experienced participants, concluding that the HIFT session elicited significant acute perturbations across all measured markers. Notably, experienced participants exhibited greater lymphocyte and cortisol responses compared to novice individuals, indicating differential physiological adaptations and stress responses to the high-intensity exercise.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: A single 'Cindy' workout session, performed as many rounds as possible (AMRAP) within 20 minutes (consisting of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, and 15 squats). Participants were categorized as novice (3–8 months experience; n=10) and experienced (≥18 months experience; n=13), with responses compared between these groups. The session occurred after a 48-hour rest, between 6:00 AM and 8:00 AM, following a standardized breakfast (320-350 cal, 20% protein, 35% fat, 45% carbohydrate). Participants abstained from specific supplements (antioxidants, caffeine, creatine, beta-alanine, nitrate, bicarbonates) before the study. Mean heart rate during exercise was 172.0 ± 8.6 bpm (93.1 ± 2.3%HR max). No direct dose-response comparisons for varying workout intensity were reported, though individual work (number of rounds) varied.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased immediately post-exercise from 6.8 to 11.8x10^3 /μL, returning to baseline within 30 min (p<0.01). Experienced participants exhibited higher post-exercise concentrations than novice ones (p<0.01), with a significant correlation to the number of rounds performed (r = 0.43; p = 0.040).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Mediates immune response and defense against infections.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Single 'Cindy' workout session (HIFT), comparison between novice and experienced participants. Acute 'Cindy' workout session, during a 24-hour recovery period.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute immune system perturbation/activation following intense exercise. Values within reference range are fundamental for optimal physical performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased post-exercise from 3.3 to 4.5x10^3 /μL and at 30 min post-exercise (p<0.01), returning to baseline by 24 h. No group differences were found, though novice participants showed a significant decrease from immediately post-exercise to 30 min post-exercise (p=0.020). Acute release partially secondary to cortisol increase.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Primary immune cell in inflammatory responses; component of innate immune response, involved in inflammation and phagocytosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Single 'Cindy' workout session (HIFT); acute 'Cindy' workout session. Following exercise, particularly noted at 30-minute after exercise, and influenced by cortisol.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute inflammatory response as part of the immune system's reaction to exercise stress. Elevated levels maintained at 30 min post-exercise in both groups suggest a sustained immune response.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, then lower (lymphocytopenia), then returned to baseline
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise (2.8 to 5.9x10^3 /μL), followed by a significant decrease (lymphocytopenia, 2.2x10^3 /μL) at 30 min post-exercise, returning to pre-exercise values by 24 h (p<0.01). Experienced participants showed significantly higher post-exercise concentrations (p=0.005) and greater overall responses (p<0.05) than novice individuals. Lymphocyte activity is inhibited by cortisol increase. Significantly correlated with the number of rounds performed (r = 0.55; p = 0.006).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Key immune cell for adaptive immunity, central to adaptive immunity, mediates adaptive immune response and immune memory.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Single 'Cindy' workout session (HIFT), comparison between novice and experienced participants. Acute 'Cindy' workout session.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute changes in adaptive immune cell distribution and potential transient immune suppression (lymphocytopenia) following intense exercise. Higher response in experienced individuals might suggest a trained immune adaptation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly at all post-exercise time points (immediately, 30 min, 24 h) from a pre-exercise level of 174.9 U.L^-1 to 226.7 U.L^-1 post-exercise (p<0.01), remaining elevated at 24 h. The highest average was 276 U/L at 24 h, with an individual maximum of 765 U/L. No significant differences in the magnitude of increase were observed between novice and experienced groups (p>0.01).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Enzyme involved in energy metabolism, released into blood upon muscle damage; marker released into circulation upon muscle cell damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Single 'Cindy' workout session (HIFT); acute 'Cindy' workout session. Post-exercise response.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute muscle tissue damage and breakdown following intense physical exertion. Observed values were well below those indicative of rhabdomyolysis (10,000–20,000 U/L), confirming that the intervention did not induce excessive muscle damage.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise (from 14.7 to 17.0 μg/dL) and at 30 min post-exercise for all participants (p<0.01). Experienced participants exhibited significantly higher concentrations both post-exercise (p=0.001) and at 30 min post-exercise (p=0.036) compared to novice participants. Novice participants' cortisol was significantly higher than pre-exercise only at 30 min post-exercise (p=0.045). Significantly correlated with the number of rounds performed (r = 0.53; p = 0.010).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Stress hormone, regulates metabolism and immune responses; a primary stress hormone involved in metabolism, immune regulation, and inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Single 'Cindy' workout session (HIFT), comparison between novice and experienced participants. Acute 'Cindy' workout session. Acute response to single CrossFit 'Cindy' workout.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute physiological stress response to intense exercise. Higher levels in experienced participants suggest greater overall work performed, and prolonged high levels following high-intensity exercise warn of potential negative health outcomes.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, then reduced but remained elevated
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise (from 1.9 to 13.5 mmol.L^-1, always exceeding 10 mmol.L^-1) and decreased by 30 min post-exercise, but remained above baseline (>2.8 mmol.L^-1) for all participants (p<0.01). No significant differences were observed between novice and experienced individuals in the magnitude of change (p<0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, indicator of metabolic stress; involved in energy metabolism, byproduct of anaerobic glycolysis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Single 'Cindy' workout session (HIFT); acute 'Cindy' workout session.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute metabolic stress and the extent of anaerobic energy contribution during high-intensity exercise, reflecting fatigue. High levels indicate significant work intensity and high anaerobic demand.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher, then returned to baseline, then higher again
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise (p<0.01), returned to pre-exercise values within 30 min post-exercise, and increased again 24 h post-protocol for all participants. No significant differences were found between groups (p<0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Part of the innate immune system, involved in phagocytosis, antigen presentation, and tissue repair.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Delayed monocytosis at 24 h post-exercise indicates ongoing immune modulation and potential involvement in tissue repair processes.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower, then higher, then returned to baseline
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased significantly immediately post-exercise compared to baseline (p<0.01), then rose above pre-exercise and post-exercise values at 30 min post-exercise (within the normal range of 0.78–3.58). Returned to pre-exercise values at 24 h. No group differences were found in NLR, but at 30 min post-exercise, it was higher than pre-exercise only for the experimental group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An indicator of systemic inflammation and physiological stress; prognostic marker with distinct meanings between healthy and disease states.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acute 'Cindy' workout session. Post-exercise, particularly when cortisol actions prevail.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Increased NLR at 30 min post-exercise, especially in the experimental group, corroborates the hypothesis that cortisol promotes a pro-neutrophil, anti-lymphocyte environment. Reflects immune modulation and physiological stress.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly post-exercise and decreased within 30 min post-exercise for all participants (p<0.01). NCR in the novice group was significantly higher post-exercise (p=0.021) than in experienced participants.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects the interaction between immediate immune and neuroendocrine stress responses; offers a view of cortisol-independent increase of neutrophils.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acute 'Cindy' workout session. Useful for 30-minute post-exercise collection due to cortisol's delayed effect on neutrophil induction.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher NCR in novice participants post-exercise suggests a differential acute stress response related to training experience.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Area Under the Curve of Cortisol

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in the experienced group compared to novice participants (p=0.004). Significant acute perturbations; significantly different from pre-exercise (p < 0.05); significantly greater than post-30min and post-24h (p < 0.05); significantly greater than post-30min (p < 0.05); significantly greater than pre-exercise only for ALL and EXP (p < 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An integrative measure of the total physiological stress response as indicated by cortisol levels over a period.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Following a single 'Cindy' HIFT workout session, with differential responses between experienced and novice participants.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the overall magnitude of the physiological stress response over time to high-intensity exercise, potentially correlating with training status or recovery.
